question:
A 25-year-old man experiencing homelessness, with a history of asthma, presents to clinic with a
persistent rash on his scalp and feet that has been present for approximately one year. He describes
the rash as dry and flaky, and reports severe nocturnal pruritus that interferes with sleep.
Over-the-counter dandruff shampoo has provided minimal relief. Physical examination reveals a scaly
alopecic patch, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and fine scaling between the toes and on the
lateral and plantar aspects of the feet. His vital signs show a temperature of 99°F (37°C), blood
pressure 106/77 mmHg, and heart rate 81/min. Which diagnostic test would provide the most accurate
diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Wood's lamp (B) Microscopic visualization of skin scraping (C) Culture
in Sabouraud liquid medium (D) KOH preparation of scalp scraping (E) Skin biopsy with PAS staining
(F) Dermoscopy of the affected area (G) Tzanck smear of the lesion (H) Direct immunofluorescence of
skin scraping (I) Gram stain of skin scraping (J) Fungal PCR assay

A. Dermoscopy of the affected area
B. Wood's lamp
C. Tzanck smear of the lesion
D. Gram stain of skin scraping
E. Fungal PCR assay
F. Culture in Sabouraud liquid medium
G. KOH preparation of scalp scraping
H. Skin biopsy with PAS staining
I. Direct immunofluorescence of skin scraping
J. Microscopic visualization of skin scraping
